title: SOC2 prep scratchpad - Oliver Park
content:
Goal: collect brain-dump of open questions, proposed controls and quick wins for SOC2 Type II readiness (focus: Redwood Private + Dedicated infra).

Context/assumptions:
- We are targeting SOC2 coverage primarily for the Private product (VPC/on-prem) and Dedicated tenants; hosted API overlap via RBAC and separation controls.
- Timeline: aim to be audit-ready for first control testing window in Q2 2026.
- Primary scope boundaries: control plane (Redwood-managed), customer data plane (customer-managed for Private), dedicated infra nodes in Dedicated offering.

Quick notes / to-do (prioritized):
- Inventory: finish asset inventory export (infra hosts, KMS, service accounts). Owner: Aisha. Jira: SEC-1123.
- Evidence backlog: start collecting deployment runbooks and change logs for last 12 months. Owner: Ryan.
- Policies: update Acceptable Use + Data Retention policy to reflect Private deployment options. Owner: me.
- Least privilege: confirm IAM roles for service accounts used by private control plane connectors.

Open risk/questions (brainstorm):
1) Data classification: do we have a lightweight mapping that says what is considered customer data vs telemetry vs logs? Where is this stored? (Confluence page exists but needs refresh).
2) Key management: for Private we support customer KMS/HSM — need clear doc about who rotates keys and how we demonstrate separation of duties to auditor.
3) Backup/restore: Dedicated customers have snapshots — need retention schedules and proof of restore testing for at least one customer.
4) Change management: engineers often push infra changes via PRs in repo infra/ops. How to map PRs -> deployment evidence for control? Do we require tagging releases with change request IDs?
5) On-call access: SRE sometimes uses sudo for emergency access. Need justification/approval log + post-incident review evidence.

Draft control mappings (very rough) — map Trust Services Criteria to internal artifacts:
- CC6.1 (Logical access): Controls = IAM role audit, periodic access reviews, MFA enforced. Evidence: IAM audit logs (Cloud), access review sheet (quarterly), Okta MFA policy screenshot. Owner: Aisha.
- CC7.1 (Encryption): Controls = in-transit TLS for all endpoints, at-rest encryption (customer-managed for Private or AWS-managed for hosted). Evidence: infra config snippets, KMS policy, architecture diagram. Owner: Security eng (TBD).
- CC3.2 (Change management): Controls = PR-based deployments, CI pipeline approvals, tagged releases. Evidence = Git history for release, deployment logs, change request tracking in Jira SEC-11xx. Owner: Ryan.
- CC5.1 (Monitoring & incident response): Controls = centralized logging (ELK/Datadog), pagerduty alerts, incident postmortems. Evidence = alert rules, last 12 mos incident list, one sanitized postmortem. Owner: SRE lead.

Evidence gaps (actionable):
- No consistent retention policy for infra logs older than 90 days — need policy + export for audit window.
- Missing formal proof of role-based access review cadence; we have ad-hoc lists but no signed attestation.
- Need documented KMS key rotation policy for Hosted vs Private (customer-managed) with dates.
- Recovery test evidence: we have snapshots but no documented restore runbook with success proof.

Immediate next steps (next 2 weeks):
- Sync with Aisha: get list of service accounts and last-used dates. (Meeting: 2026-02-22)
- Create an evidence tracker spreadsheet (sheet link placeholder) and start uploading artifacts per control. Owner: Oliver.
- Draft a short one-pager on key management differences for Private vs Hosted — to use in auditor kickoff. Owner: Oliver.
- Assign change management mapping task to infra lead to tag last 6 months of releases with Jira change IDs.

Notes to self / fragments: 
- Auditor likely to ask for separation of duties for deploy -> ops -> security. Prepare org chart + approvals.
- For customer-managed KMS, we should capture a template statement customers can sign acknowledging responsibilities.
- Consider small tabletop DR test for Dedicated in March to generate restore evidence.

References / links I keep wanting to check:
- Confluence: SOC2 checklist (update needed) -> https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SEC/SOC2+Overview
- Jira: SEC-1123 (asset inventory), SEC-1187 (evidence collection), SEC-1201 (DR test)
- Slack: #security-audit pinned notes (search: auditor kickoff Jan 2026)
- Infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/452 (example deploy change)

Rough timeline (high level):
- Feb: finalize scope + inventory, start evidence collection (low hanging fruit).
- Mar: tabletop DR, complete access review artifacts, policy updates.
- Apr: consolidate artifacts, remediation of gaps.
- May: internal pre-audit and auditor kickoff.

Misc formatting reminders: keep evidence filenames standardized: <control>-<artifact-type>-<YYYYMMDD> (e.g., CC6-iam-audit-20260215.pdf).

Unresolved decisions (to decide with leadership):
- Scope endpoints: include hosted API logs in scope? (pros: shows overall maturity; cons: extra evidence burden).
- Level of customer evidence acceptance for Private deployments (do we accept customer-provided attestation?).

End of scratchpad. Will clean up and split into proper Confluence doc after initial syncs.

-- Oliver
